feature: One layer lines up inside its screen
summary: Align used to need two layers. Now one box sitting on a screen can be lined up against the screen, so a single press puts a label in the middle of a card.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Needs Screens and Align, both on by default.

try.do: Press F and drag out a screen about 400 by 360.
Press R and draw a small box near the screen's top left corner.
Press V. The inspector should now show an Arrange row with six live buttons and a line naming the screen.
Click the third align button in the top row's left group (Align Center). The box jumps to the middle across.
Click the middle button of the right group (Align Middle). The box is now dead centre of the screen.
Press Command Z twice. Each press puts one of those two back.
Draw a second box on the screen, shift-click both, and read the line under the buttons: two layers line up with each other, not with the screen.
Press Command G to group them, double click into the group, and click one piece. The Arrange row is gone on purpose.

evaluate: With one layer picked, does the line under the buttons tell you what is about to move, before you press anything?
Is centring on the screen what you expected Align Center to mean there, or did you expect the picture's middle?
Two layers picked still line up with each other rather than with the screen around them. Is that the switch you would predict?
A piece inside a group on a screen gets no Arrange row at all. Would you rather it lined up inside its group?
Does one press per undo feel right, or would you want both centring presses to come back together?
rough: Align is a move, not a rule. Centre a box on a screen and the Layout section right underneath still reads Left and Top, so dragging the screen wider slides the box back off centre. Making an align press write a lasting rule was deliberately not done, because a button that silently changes a setting is a surprise, but the two sections sitting next to each other saying different things is the weakest part of this.

A piece inside a plain group has no reference and shows no Arrange row. Lining a word up inside the button that holds it is the obvious next want and is filed as a follow-up: it needs the group's own box and a rule for a group of one, whose box is the piece itself and whose buttons would do nothing.

The line reads 'This layer lines up inside Frame' for a screen still carrying its default name, which is a little stiff. It reads properly once the screen is named, and screens are named by clicking their label.
Screen Recording was granted, so all three pictures are real window captures from the probe app, not offscreen renders.
Spacing evenly against a screen's inner edges is not offered. Two boxes plus two screen edges has two readings and nobody asked for it yet.
